name: Act of March 2, 1889: the Cheyenne River reservation (Royce 703)
citation: Act of March 2, 1889, ch. 405, 25 Stat. 888 (in force by proclamation of February 10, 1890)
nations: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe (Mnicoujou, Oohenumpa, Itazipco and Sihasapa Lakota)
promises: The Act set apart for the Indians receiving rations at the Cheyenne River agency the lands between the Missouri, the Cheyenne River, the 102nd meridian and the Standing Rock line (Royce).

The Act of March 2, 1889 divided the Great Sioux Reservation into separate reservations; section 21 opened the rest to sale for the benefit of the Sioux, and section 19 kept in force all provisions of the 1868 treaty and the 1877 agreement not in conflict with it (Court of Claims, 105 Ct. Cl. 725).
today: In 1946 the Court of Claims held that the United States illegally charged food rations it owed the Sioux under the 1877 agreement, and certain agency costs, against Cheyenne River trust funds (case C-531 (23)); those funds came from land sales under later Acts (1895 to 1910). It allowed $751,784.25 but set the recoveries off against reimbursable expenditures under section 17 of the 1889 Act and dismissed all seven petitions, so nothing was paid (105 Ct. Cl. 725). The Supreme Court vacated that judgment and remanded the cases on December 16, 1946 to consider the Indian Claims Commission Act; the Court of Claims re-entered it unchanged on June 28, 1948 (112 Ct. Cl. 50), and certiorari was denied in 1949 (as cited in ICC Docket 119, 34 Ind. Cl. Comm. 230). That ruling concerns the 1877 ration duty and the later sale funds, not this reservation's land under the 1889 Act, so it is not counted as a breach of this record. In 1957 the Indian Claims Commission dismissed a Cheyenne River claim that lands sold under the Act of May 29, 1908 had been wrongly classed as non-coal lands (Docket 192), a ruling for the United States.

nationVoice.summary: The history the Tribe publishes says the 1889 Act set the reservation boundaries, and that as land was ceded the agency town had to move because it fell outside them.

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): removed the court-ruling breach on 105 Ct. Cl. 725 and moved it to today. The opinion grounds the illegal charges in article 5 of the 1877 agreement (19 Stat. 254) and the trust funds of the 1895 to 1910 sale Acts; the 1889 Act appears only through section 19 and as the source of the offsets. The 1946 judgment was vacated and re-entered unchanged in 1948 (112 Ct. Cl. 50). Status lowered to no-breach-found.

The 1889 Act itself and the land ceded under it are recorded under cession-1889-03-02-sioux (Royce 631 and 699). This Royce row is the reservation kept. It is not marked sameEventAs that record because this row is the land kept, not the land ceded.
Later reductions of this reservation by Acts of Congress after 1889 are not in Royce's schedule and are not researched here.
The ICC accounting dockets for each reservation (114 to 119) were seen in the index but not read for this record.
The Tribe's history PDF was read through the primary record's citation, not reloaded in this pass.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Sioux, Cheyenne River 1889; the Sioux accounting dockets (114, 1963; 115 to 118, 1974) rule on accounting exceptions and record the Court of Claims holding that 1889 Act obligations were met by 1925, with no liability finding; nothing new.
